fyNote: Financial year ends 31 December. 2025 includes a one-off RM11.3bn gain from selling the airlines to AirAsia X.
segmentNote: After the airline sale, Capital A owns logistics, engineering, travel-app, digital and food businesses that mainly serve the AirAsia airlines (AR p.21).

how.title: How Capital A makes money now
how.text: Revenue = fees from aircraft maintenance (ADE) + parcel and cargo delivery (Teleport) + travel bookings (MOVE) + food (Santan) + digital services
facts: Still under PN17, awaiting Bursa's decision to exit (AR p.21)

story.scale_label: logistics, engineering, travel app, digital and food

growth.profitNote: Profit jumped on a one-off RM11.3bn gain from the airline sale, so a growth figure is not meaningful.

pnl.period: FY2025, continuing businesses before the one-off gain

items.label: Other operating costs
items.tip: Offices, marketing, IT and other running costs.

items.label: Staff costs
items.tip: Salaries for engineers, logistics and digital staff.

items.label: Logistic expenses
items.tip: Trucking, air freight and last-mile delivery paid by Teleport.

items.label: Consumables
items.tip: Aircraft parts and materials used in maintenance.

items.label: Depreciation
items.tip: Wear and tear on equipment, hangars and leased buildings.

items.label: Finance costs
items.tip: Interest on about RM1.3bn of borrowings.

items.label: Tax and other
items.tip: Tax and a small derivative loss.

items.label: Loss before the one-off gain
items.tip: Without the RM11.3bn disposal gain, the businesses Capital A still owns spent more than they earned in 2025.

pnl.incomeNote: Costs exceeded revenue: about RM143 was spent for every RM100 earned. The RM11.3bn one-off gain and the airlines' profit until handover are left out here.

fiveYear.note: Only two comparable years: earlier reports included the airlines. 2025 profit includes the one-off RM11.3bn gain.

rows.name: Teleport (logistics)
rows.tip: Air cargo and e-commerce parcel delivery: 348,000 tonnes and 167 million parcels in 2025.

rows.name: ADE (aircraft engineering)
rows.tip: Aircraft maintenance and heavy checks for AirAsia and other airlines.

rows.name: AirAsia MOVE (travel app)
rows.tip: Online travel bookings: flights, hotels and duty-free; 17.3 million monthly users.

rows.name: AirAsia Next (digital)
rows.tip: Digital, data and brand services for the AirAsia ecosystem.

rows.name: Santan (food)
rows.tip: Inflight meals and food sold through retail partners.

segments.note: Segment revenue includes sales to other Capital A companies; profit before tax excludes head-office items and the one-off disposal gain (AR p.149).

balance.note: After the airline sale, equity turned positive (RM921m) from a RM10bn deficit. Two-thirds of assets are money owed by related AirAsia companies (RM5.1bn), so collecting it matters.

waterfall.l: Cash from operations (incl. airlines until handover)
Airlines' investing and financing until handover
Airline cash handed over on disposal

cash.wfNote: Most of the cash came from the airlines before they were handed over and went back into airline lease and debt payments. The businesses Capital A keeps produced RM451m of operating cash.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM1.1 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (FY2025 profit)
metrics.plain: Not meaningful for 2025: profit is almost all a one-off RM11.3bn gain from handing the airlines to AirAsia X; without it the remaining businesses made a loss.

metrics.label: EPS (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Not meaningful for 2025: profit is almost all a one-off RM11.3bn gain from handing the airlines to AirAsia X; without it the remaining businesses made a loss.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 dividends)
metrics.plain: No cash dividend for 2025. Shareholders received AirAsia X shares as a dividend in specie (AR p.25).

metrics.label: Payout ratio FY2025
metrics.plain: No cash dividend; shareholders received AirAsia X shares instead.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.1 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity FY2025
metrics.plain: Not meaningful: shareholders' equity was negative (RM-8.8bn) at the start of 2025.

metrics.label: Net margin FY2025
metrics.plain: Not meaningful for 2025: profit is almost all a one-off RM11.3bn gain from handing the airlines to AirAsia X; without it the remaining businesses made a loss.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Profit growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Not meaningful for 2025: profit is almost all a one-off RM11.3bn gain from handing the airlines to AirAsia X; without it the remaining businesses made a loss.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM0.85 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 92% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Free cash flow FY2025
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM288 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: Loss of continuing businesses before the one-off gain
metrics.plain: Revenue minus all costs of the businesses Capital A still owns, before the RM11.3bn disposal gain (AR p.98-99).

drivers.evidence: Airlines moved to AirAsia X in December 2025, with an RM11.3bn gain (AR p.93, p.21)
drivers.why: Removes the airline's large debts and turns equity positive.

drivers.evidence: Regularisation plan done; awaiting Bursa Malaysia's decision to lift PN17 (AR p.21)
drivers.why: Exiting PN17 would remove a major overhang on the shares.

drivers.evidence: Equity of RM921m vs a RM10.0bn deficit a year earlier (AR p.101)
drivers.why: A healthier starting point for the remaining businesses.

drivers.evidence: Revenue +25% to RM894m with more third-party customers (AR p.21)
drivers.why: A profitable business that can grow beyond AirAsia.

drivers.evidence: Revenue +14% to RM1.2bn; turned a RM21m loss into an operating profit (AR p.21)
Revenue over RM485m; Q4 revenue tripled quarter on quarter (AR p.21)
drivers.why: Shows the app can earn from more than AirAsia flights.

drivers.evidence: Continuing businesses lost about RM795m before the disposal gain (AR p.98-99)
drivers.why: Head-office and financing costs still outweigh business profits.

drivers.evidence: RM5.1bn due from related parties at year-end (AR p.100)
drivers.why: Depends on the airlines' ability to pay.

drivers.evidence: Borrowings of RM1.28bn vs RM433m of cash (AR p.100-101)
drivers.why: Interest costs weigh on a still-small business.

drivers.evidence: Most businesses serve the AirAsia airlines (AR p.21)
drivers.why: Their volumes rise and fall with airline capacity.

drivers.evidence: P/E not meaningful; about 1.1 times book value at RM0.24 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: The price reflects uncertainty about the new, smaller group.

competitors.name: Grab, Traveloka, Agoda
competitors.how: Travel booking and super-apps competing with AirAsia MOVE
competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

competitors.name: DHL, J&T Express, Pos Malaysia
competitors.how: Parcel and cargo logistics competing with Teleport

outlook.text: Restored to positive equity of RM921m; non-aviation businesses grew revenue 13% to RM3.18bn (AR p.21).
First two goals of the regularisation plan achieved (AR p.21).
Awaiting Bursa Malaysia's decision on exiting PN17 (AR p.21).
Management says the group is not completely out of the woods: still under PN17, and AirAsia has aircraft waiting to return to service (AR p.20).

outlookOverall.text: Management sees the airline sale as a turning point but says the group is not yet out of the woods (AR p.20-21).
